scope: THE DECISION THAT SETS STATE 3: an 8-byte comparison at [obj+0x5FC] against a value in the caller's frame - it reads like a session token check

the_code_at_0xba3c05.0xBA3C05: push 8 ; lea edx,[ebp-0xC] ; lea eax,[esi+0x5FC] ; push eax
the_code_at_0xba3c05.0xBA3C12: call 0xB73FE0 - compare 8 bytes at [obj+0x5FC] with the 8 bytes at [ebp-0xC]
the_code_at_0xba3c05.0xBA3C1A: test eax,eax ; jne 0xBA3C62 - if not equal, take the other branch (which sets something else and returns)
the_code_at_0xba3c05.0xBA3C21: cmp [obj+0x644], 0 ; jne 0xBA3C38 - if the flag is already set, skip the call

what_that_means: state 3 is entered when an 8-byte value stored at [obj+0x5FC] equals an 8-byte value supplied by the caller
an 8-byte equality check on a connection object is most naturally a session id or handshake token
so the client reaches state 3 when its token matches the one the caller compares against, and our client IS at state 3 - so that comparison already succeeded
which means state 3 is not the failure point: it is the state the client is in after a successful token comparison, and something must then move it onward
what_this_implies_for_the_remaining_work: the state machine around 0xBA3xxx is a session state machine: 0 idle, 1/2 intermediate, 3 token-matched-and-waiting
the transition out of 3 is the one that has not been located
and because state 3 is reached by a successful 8-byte comparison, the missing transition is most likely gated on a further message or on a timer rather than on the token
